# Shared UI catalog

Everything you may build with, all imported from `@misty/ui`. If it isn't listed here it doesn't
exist: add it to @misty/ui first (see DESIGN.md), then regenerate this file. Read the source file before
using a component for the first time; its props are the contract.

## Controls

| Export | What it is for | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BackButton` | Going back to the previous page or step: the arrow and the word, as one quiet button. | controls/BackButton.tsx |
| `Button` | _No doc comment yet._ | controls/Button.tsx |
| `Checkbox` | _No doc comment yet._ | controls/Checkbox.tsx |
| `ChoiceGroup` | The one segmented control: mutually exclusive choices on a track, such as a view mode or Month/Agenda. It is a radio group, so the chosen option is the tab stop and arrow keys, Home and End move the choice. The whole control, track included, is one control height, so it lines up with buttons in the same row. | controls/ChoiceGroup.tsx |
| `ChoiceList` | A vertical list of choices split by hairlines, with a checkmark on each picked row: one pick (a radio group) or several (`multiple`). For questions an agent asks, quiz answers and other pick-from-these lists whose rows carry a line of description. Short sets of mutually exclusive options in a bar use ChoiceGroup instead. | controls/ChoiceList.tsx |
| `ChoiceTile` | One choice in a grid of pictures, such as an agent's avatar or a Space's emoji. The picked tile is filled; the rest wash on hover. Put a set of them in a grid with an accessible name. | controls/ChoiceTile.tsx |
| `ColorChip` | A color shown, not picked: a small square of it beside a value such as `rgb(…)`, so the value reads as the color it is. A faint inner edge keeps it visible on a fill of the same color. | controls/ColorSwatch.tsx |
| `ColorSwatch` | One pickable color. Pens, highlighters, and backgrounds all use these. | controls/ColorSwatch.tsx |
| `CustomColorSwatch` | Opens the system color picker; sits after a row of ColorSwatches, at their size. | controls/ColorSwatch.tsx |
| `CopyButton` | The one copy button: an IconButton whose icon turns into a check for a moment after it copies, with no words. With `value` it writes that text to the clipboard and says so in a notice if the clipboard refuses; with `onCopy` the caller copies. | controls/CopyButton.tsx |
| `DisclosureButton` | Shows or hides more of a list under it, such as More engines: a quiet, muted button at the start of its row with a chevron that turns as it opens. The caller mounts what it shows. | controls/DisclosureButton.tsx |
| `DragHandleButton` | An icon button that lives inside an HTML5-draggable surface (editor block handles, pinned rows). WebKit will not start a drag from a `user-select: none` element, so this gives back the text selection Button turns off; otherwise it is the quiet 27px IconButton. | controls/DragHandleButton.tsx |
| `Field` | Label, control and its error, wired for assistive technology. Forms use this. | controls/Field.tsx |
| `FieldError` | A field's error, under its control. Field draws this itself; use it directly beside a custom control, giving the control `aria-describedby={id}` and `aria-invalid`. | controls/Field.tsx |
| `FileInput` | A hidden native file picker. Open it from a visible Button via the forwarded ref (`ref.current?.click()`); it has no look of its own. | controls/FileInput.tsx |
| `IconButton` | The one icon-only button. Its label is its accessible name and its Tooltip, with the shortcut after it while shortcut hints are on; it never uses the system title. The icon is its child and draws at 18px. With `asChild` it styles its child, such as a router Link. | controls/IconButton.tsx |
| `InlineLink` | A link inside a line of text, such as the terms in a page's small print: underlined, in the text's own color, brightening on hover. It is a button; the caller opens the page. With `asChild` it styles a real link instead. | controls/InlineLink.tsx |
| `Input` | _No doc comment yet._ | controls/Input.tsx |
| `SearchField` | Misty's one search box: a filled field with no hairline, in the same 36px frame as the selects, buttons and chips beside it, so a bar of them lines up. It brightens under the pointer and takes a soft neutral edge while typing in it. A clear button shows once there is text, and Escape clears it too. | controls/SearchField.tsx |
| `SecretField` | A secret such as an API key, in one control the size of an empty 36px Input. Empty, it is a password field that saves on Enter or when it loses focus. Saved, it reads "Saved in keychain" beside a lock, with a ⋯ inside its right edge that offers Replace key and Remove key (which asks first). The saved value is never shown or read back. Errors show under the field. | controls/SecretField.tsx |
| `Segment` | One of a few choices that keeps the role its group gives it: a tab in a tablist, a radio in a radiogroup, or a toggle. The chosen one (`aria-selected` or `aria-checked`) is filled and bright; the rest are muted and brighten under the pointer. For a plain choice of one value out of a few, ChoiceGroup is the one control; Segment is for a bar whose parts differ in kind, such as the Studio's dock (modes as tabs, the camera as radios, sounds as a toggle). | controls/Segment.tsx |
| `SegmentTrack` | The faint track a row of `track` Segments sits in. Give it the group's role and name. | controls/Segment.tsx |
| `ShortcutField` | One command's shortcut, recorded in an ordinary 36px field. Clicking it or pressing Enter starts recording ("Press keys", with a red dot); the next chord becomes the binding, Escape cancels, and Tab or a click elsewhere leaves it as it was. The chord reads in the sans font (⇧⌘K), and the × clears it. A conflict or a reserved chord shows under the field. One field per command. | controls/ShortcutField.tsx |
| `Label` | _No doc comment yet._ | controls/Label.tsx |
| `OptionSelect` | A Select built from a plain options list; the shared replacement for a native <select>. | controls/OptionSelect.tsx |
| `Select` | _No doc comment yet._ Parts: `SelectContent`, `SelectTrigger`, `SelectValue`. | controls/Select.tsx |
| `SelectItem` | One choice in a Select: icon · label, with a checkmark at the right edge while picked. | controls/Select.tsx |
| `Slider` | _No doc comment yet._ | controls/Slider.tsx |
| `SplitButton` | A button and the menu of its other choices joined into one control: the main action first (an IconButton or Button), then a MenuTrigger with just its chevron, narrowed to the chevron and meeting the button with no gap or corner between them. The group is named by `label`. | controls/SplitButton.tsx |
| `Switch` | _No doc comment yet._ | controls/Switch.tsx |
| `Textarea` | _No doc comment yet._ | controls/Textarea.tsx |
| `Pressable` | A clickable surface whose content is its look: a card, a calendar event, a tab, a canvas item. It adds button semantics and disabled handling, and with `wash` one of the shared hover looks; otherwise the content draws its own hover and focus states, since focus rings are off app-wide. Anything that looks like a button uses Button or IconButton instead. | controls/Pressable.tsx |
| `RowTools` | A row's own buttons, at its end, as one tight group: IconButtons 27px, 2.25px apart, so the row's 4.5px inset shows around them and no gap opens between icons. The row is a `group/row`. | controls/RowTools.tsx |

## Overlays

| Export | What it is for | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FloatingPip` | A picture-in-picture: a small live picture floating over its container (the nearest positioned ancestor), moved like the system's own. Drag it anywhere; let go and it glides to the nearest corner, where it stays. A press opens what it shows; let go past the right edge and it docks. Its controls show on hover, over the picture, and a white ring breathes around it while something in it works. | overlays/FloatingPip.tsx |
| `useOverlaySide` | _No doc comment yet._ | overlays/OverlaySide.tsx |
| `AlertDialog` | _No doc comment yet._ Parts: `AlertDialogContent`, `AlertDialogDescription`, `AlertDialogHeader`, `AlertDialogTitle`. | overlays/AlertDialog.tsx |
| `AlertDialogAction` | The dialog's action, a 36px button. A delete uses ConfirmDeleteDialog instead of building one from these parts. | overlays/AlertDialog.tsx |
| `AlertDialogCancel` | Cancel: a quiet 36px button. | overlays/AlertDialog.tsx |
| `AlertDialogFooter` | Buttons at the end of the dialog, right-aligned: Cancel, then the action. | overlays/AlertDialog.tsx |
| `Command` | _No doc comment yet._ Parts: `CommandGroup`, `CommandInput`, `CommandList`, `CommandSeparator`. | overlays/Command.tsx |
| `CommandEmpty` | The one muted line when nothing matches the search. | overlays/Command.tsx |
| `CommandItem` | One row of a Command list. | overlays/Command.tsx |
| `CommandPaletteInput` | The palette's search box: the body role in the bright text, a muted placeholder, no frame. | overlays/CommandPalette.tsx |
| `CommandPaletteItem` | One row of the palette: 45px, the meta role, with large corners; the row cmdk has picked takes the control wash and the bright text. | overlays/CommandPalette.tsx |
| `CommandPaletteList` | The palette's list: it scrolls, and its group headings are muted captions. | overlays/CommandPalette.tsx |
| `CommandPalette` | The palette itself, holding its input, list and rows: a column with no look of its own, since the dialog around it is the panel. It takes cmdk's props (`shouldFilter`, `loop`, `value`). | overlays/CommandPalette.tsx |
| `CommandPaletteGroup` | A group of the palette's rows under its `heading`, drawn as the list's muted caption. | overlays/CommandPalette.tsx |
| `CommandPaletteMatch` | The part of a row's text that matches what was typed: a faint wash in the bright text. | overlays/CommandPalette.tsx |
| `CommandPaletteTab` | One of the palette's type tabs (All, Chats, Docs…): 31.5px, the meta role, muted until hovered; the picked one (`aria-selected`) takes the control wash and the bright text. | overlays/CommandPalette.tsx |
| `ConfirmDeleteDialog` | Every delete asks first in this small dialog: what goes, then Cancel (quiet) and the danger Delete. There is no corner ×; Escape and Cancel close it. | overlays/ConfirmDeleteDialog.tsx |
| `useConfirmDelete` | The same dialog for call sites that ask in the middle of a handler. Render `dialog` once in the component; `confirm(options)` opens it and resolves true once the delete is done (or, without `onConfirm`, once Delete is chosen), and false when it is cancelled. | overlays/ConfirmDeleteDialog.tsx |
| `ContextMenu` | _No doc comment yet._ Parts: `ContextMenuCheckboxItem`, `ContextMenuContent`, `ContextMenuGroup`, `ContextMenuItem`, `ContextMenuLabel`, `ContextMenuRadioGroup`, `ContextMenuRadioItem`, `ContextMenuSeparator`, `ContextMenuSub`, `ContextMenuSubContent`, `ContextMenuSubTrigger`, `ContextMenuTrigger`. | overlays/ContextMenu.tsx |
| `Dialog` | _No doc comment yet._ Parts: `DialogClose`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogHeader`, `DialogTitle`. | overlays/Dialog.tsx |
| `DialogBody` | The dialog's content between its header and footer. With `layout="scroll"` (and always at `size="media"`) it takes the height that's left and scrolls on its own, edge to edge, while the header and footer stay put. In the default flow it is a plain block. | overlays/Dialog.tsx |
| `DialogFooter` | The dialog's buttons, right-aligned at 36px: a quiet Cancel, then its one primary action. | overlays/Dialog.tsx |
| `DropdownMenu` | _No doc comment yet._ Parts: `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`, `DropdownMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuRadioGroup`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`, `DropdownMenuSub`, `DropdownMenuSubContent`, `DropdownMenuSubTrigger`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`. | overlays/DropdownMenu.tsx |
| `MenuCheckItem` | A row that turns something on or off, with a checkmark at its right edge while on. | overlays/MenuItem.tsx |
| `MenuGroup` | Groups rows for assistive tech, in either kind of menu. | overlays/MenuItem.tsx |
| `MenuIconSlot` | Draws a row's icon from either form. Also used by Select, Command and SuggestionList rows. | overlays/MenuItem.tsx |
| `MenuItem` | The one menu row: icon · label · shortcut. Works inside a DropdownMenu or a ContextMenu. | overlays/MenuItem.tsx |
| `MenuLabel` | A muted heading over a group of rows, in either kind of menu. | overlays/MenuItem.tsx |
| `MenuRadioGroup` | A set of MenuRadioItems where exactly one is picked, such as a sort order. Its rows are text alone unless each has an icon of its own: a list of efforts or models, each with the same mark, reads better without them. | overlays/MenuItem.tsx |
| `MenuRadioItem` | One choice in a MenuRadioGroup, with a checkmark at its right edge while picked. A choice shows no shortcut: the menu is where it is picked, not where its key is learned. | overlays/MenuItem.tsx |
| `MenuSeparator` | A hairline between groups of rows, in either kind of menu. | overlays/MenuItem.tsx |
| `MenuSubmenu` | A row that opens a nested menu; the right chevron comes from the sub-trigger. | overlays/MenuItem.tsx |
| `MenuChevron` | The chevron on anything that opens a menu or popover. It turns over while its trigger is open (the trigger carries `data-state="open"`), so every dropdown moves the same way. | overlays/MenuChevron.tsx |
| `MenuTrigger` | The button that opens a DropdownMenu, or a Popover with kind="popover". Labeled triggers end in a chevron unless `chevron={false}`. Features never draw their own. | overlays/MenuTrigger.tsx |
| `InfoCorner` | A quiet "i" about a surface, last in its BottomBar (the window's, a popup's or an overlay's), and the small panel it opens: a title, a line, and one action. It never floats over content. | overlays/InfoCorner.tsx |
| `PickerList` | A picker's rows under its search, or a flush popover's list: 4.5px in, scrolling. | overlays/Popover.tsx |
| `PickerSearch` | A picker's search: the popover's top row, a line under it. Pair with `kind="flush"`. | overlays/Popover.tsx |
| `Popover` | _No doc comment yet._ Parts: `PopoverAnchor`, `PopoverClose`, `PopoverContent`, `PopoverTrigger`. | overlays/Popover.tsx |
| `PopoverActions` | A panel's buttons, at its end on the right: quiet ones first, the action last. | overlays/Popover.tsx |
| `PopoverBody` | A panel's own content between its line and its actions (a field, a list of rows, a meter), set a step apart from the text above it. | overlays/Popover.tsx |
| `PopoverHeader` | A panel's first row: its title, a muted detail at the end (a count, a total), and the button that closes it. Leave `close` off only where the panel closes itself as you act in it. | overlays/Popover.tsx |
| `PopoverText` | A panel's line about itself, muted, wrapping. | overlays/Popover.tsx |
| `Portal` | Renders children into `container` (default: document.body), outside the parent's clipping. | overlays/Portal.tsx |
| `RowActions` | A row's one place for its actions: a 27px ⋯ at its right end, shown while the row is hovered, holds focus, or has a menu open, and the same menu on a right-click anywhere on the row. Put it last inside the row; the row is its nearest ancestor with the `group/row` class, which is how ListRow and tiles are built. | overlays/RowActions.tsx |
| `SearchablePicker` | A picker with a search field over its options: a trigger that shows the pick, and a list where typing narrows the rows, the current one checked, actions after a separator. For lists long enough to search (branches, folders, models); short fixed choices use OptionSelect. | overlays/SearchablePicker.tsx |
| `Sheet` | _No doc comment yet._ Parts: `SheetContent`, `SheetDescription`, `SheetTitle`. | overlays/Sheet.tsx |
| `SuggestionItem` | One option in a SuggestionList: icon · label · detail, like a menu row. | overlays/SuggestionList.tsx |
| `SuggestionList` | The popup under a combobox field (composer mentions, search boxes). Focus stays in the field, so rows are options highlighted by `selected` rather than focusable menu items. | overlays/SuggestionList.tsx |
| `Tooltip` | `<Tooltip content="New chat" shortcut="⌘N"><Button … /></Tooltip>` | overlays/Tooltip.tsx |
| `TooltipProvider` | Mounted once at the app root, with the shortcut hints setting passed in. | overlays/Tooltip.tsx |
| `Tour` | A short guided tour over the window: the rest dims, one control at a time is lit, and a card beside it says what it is for, with Back, Next and Skip. Steps whose control isn't on screen are left out. Escape skips, the arrow keys step. `onClose` says whether the person reached the end, so a caller can remember the tour was seen either way. | overlays/Tour.tsx |
| `ViewportLayer` | A viewport-sized surface for non-modal floating UI (command panels) or full-window takeovers. Modal content belongs in Dialog, Sheet, or WorkspaceOverlay instead. | overlays/ViewportLayer.tsx |
| `WorkspaceOverlay` | Shared modal shell for the full-page workspaces that are presented as overlays (Settings, Account, Remotes). Handles the portal, the Escape key, and dismiss-on-backdrop-click so each caller only supplies its own content. | overlays/WorkspaceOverlay.tsx |

## Layout

| Export | What it is for | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ActionBar` | The toolbar that gives way instead of wrapping or scrolling. It stays one control high, and when it runs out of room it gives way in a fixed order: labels turn into icons (lowest priority first), then the one `shrink` item fades down to its minimum width, then the lowest priority items fold into a trailing ⋯ menu with the same icons and labels. Every bar of actions in the app is one of these. | layout/ActionBar.tsx |
| `Collapsible` | _No doc comment yet._ Parts: `CollapsibleContent`, `CollapsibleTrigger`. | layout/Collapsible.tsx |
| `Disclosure` | A heading that opens to more under it: a page's questions and answers, a release's notes, a group of links in a docs sidebar. The whole heading is the button, with a chevron at its end that turns over while open. Put several sections in a DisclosureList to split them by hairlines. A "show more" under a list is DisclosureButton; a fold with a trigger of its own is Collapsible. | layout/Disclosure.tsx |
| `DisclosureList` | Disclosure sections one under another, split by hairlines. | layout/Disclosure.tsx |
| `FloatingPanel` | A translucent panel floating over a full-color scene, which shows through it blurred; Misty's own panes are flat. The content may be in full color. It is no dialog: it doesn't trap focus or block the scene behind it. | layout/FloatingPanel.tsx |
| `OverflowFadeText` | Long text (names, models, paths, branches) shortens with a fade at its end, never an ellipsis. The fade appears only while the text doesn't fit, and follows the label as its box or text changes. This is the default for every label in shared components. | layout/OverflowFadeText.tsx |
| `PageEnter` | Content that fades and rises into place as a page opens, such as a signed-out page's form or a setup step's title. Give it a `key` that changes to play it again. `className` is for layout. | layout/PageEnter.tsx |
| `PageHeader` | A page's top band: 54px (`--ui-header`) with a hairline under it, the title on the left and the page's actions on the right. The title fades first, down to a short stub, and only then do the actions give way. It never wraps. Without a title it is only the actions, at its end, with no hairline: the page's controls, not a bar. | layout/PageHeader.tsx |
| `ViewHeader` | The band at the top of every view of a Space: 54px (`--ui-header`), the title on the left and the view's icon buttons on the right, with no line under it, since the panes read as one sheet. It holds no search box and no create button. The title fades first, and only then do the buttons give way. It never wraps. | layout/ViewHeader.tsx |
| `BottomBar` | The bar along the bottom of the window, a popup or an overlay, which keeps room there so nothing floats over the content. A hairline along its top sets it off from the content, the way a top bar's closes it. It is lighter than a top bar: compact by default (36px, its buttons 27px), or `standard` (45px, its buttons 36px) where the person chose that for the window's bar. Its controls are centered in it, 13.5px in from the right, the "i" for the surface's tour last. `start` holds anything that belongs at its other end. When the two ends don't fit side by side, the bar scrolls sideways (SidewaysScroll) rather than shrink its items or let one end slide over the other. | layout/BottomBar.tsx |
| `TopBar` | The bar along the top of an overlay or a popup, the twin of `BottomBar`: the header's height (`--ui-header`) on the surface's own background, so its controls (a close button, last) have a band of their own and the content scrolls beneath it instead of under them. `start` holds anything that belongs at its other end, such as a title. `divider` draws a page header's hairline under it, so a bar the content scrolls beneath reads as staying put, and adds 4.5px above and below so what it holds centers between the edge and that line. | layout/TopBar.tsx |
| `DocsLayout` | A documentation site's page in three panels, as Vercel's docs are: the section's navigation on the left, the article in the middle and "On this page" on the right, under a header that stays put. The two side panels stay in view while the article scrolls; under 52rem the navigation goes (the header's own menu takes over) and under 62rem the contents do. `header` is a `DocsHeader`, `nav` the rows of the open section, `toc` a `DocsToc`, and the article's own footer (a `DocsPager`) goes last in `children`. The page is `--docs-max` wide (90rem) with `--docs-gutter` at its sides (none), so a site sets them to match its own pages. Everything that stays in view sits below `--docs-bar` too (the header's height by default, 0 where the site's own bar replaces it), and below `--docs-top` (0 by default), so a site with its own bar above (a navbar) sets it to that bar's height. Only for a docs site; the app's pages use their own layouts. | layout/DocsLayout.tsx |
| `DocsHeader` | The docs site's top band: its name, a slash, and the name of the docs you are in as a menu that switches between them (Guides, SDK, Design system…), with the open one checked; `children` (search, theme, links) sit at the end. It stays at the top while the page scrolls, on the page's own color with a hairline under it. `title` names the docs when none is open, such as on the front page. | layout/DocsLayout.tsx |
| `DocsSwitcher` | A slash and the name of the docs you are in as a menu that switches between them, with the open one checked. `DocsHeader` holds it; a site whose own bar carries the docs' controls (a navbar) puts it there instead. | layout/DocsLayout.tsx |
| `DocsTitle` | The top of a docs page: an eyebrow (its section), the title large and tightly set, and the lead under it. Docs only: its sizes are the docs' own, bigger than the app's `display` role. | layout/DocsLayout.tsx |
| `DocsHero` | A docs site's front page opening: a very large title, the lead, its buttons (`actions`), and a panel beside it on wide screens (`aside`, usually a `CodeBlock` with a `header`). Docs only. | layout/DocsLayout.tsx |
| `DocsCard` | One card on a docs page that links somewhere: its icon over a title and a line, on a hairline edge that washes under the pointer. Put them in a grid, two to a row. | layout/DocsLayout.tsx |
| `DocsToc` | "On this page": the article's own sections as a column of links that stays in view beside it, the one being read in the bright text and the rest muted. `onSelect` scrolls to a section; the caller decides which is `active`. | layout/DocsLayout.tsx |
| `DocsPager` | The links to the pages either side of this one, along the article's bottom edge: they stay on screen as the page scrolls, over a fade of the page's own color, so the next page is always one press away. Put it last in the `DocsLayout`'s children. | layout/DocsLayout.tsx |
| `DocsSearch` | The docs' search: a bordered field at the top of the sidebar that says "Search docs" with its ⌘K hint, and opens the same palette as Misty's own search (an input, a hairline, then rows under their headings) where typing narrows every page by name. Press ⌘K (or Ctrl+K) anywhere to open it. Picking a result calls `onSelect` and closes it. | layout/DocsLayout.tsx |
| `PathLine` | Where something works, as one quiet line: "Space › folder › branch" under the composer. Each segment fades instead of wrapping, and the longest name shortens first. Segments with a menu or a picker open it, like a branch switcher; a segment with `onSelect` is a quiet button that runs it, like a folder in a file's path. The line is sans; paths are never set in monospace here. It is not a breadcrumb bar of buttons across a page's top: it stays one quiet line. | layout/PathLine.tsx |
| `PathField` | A file manager's path bar, as Kura's and Explorer's: the open folder's path in a filled field, each folder a quiet button that opens it with a chevron between them, the last one bright. A long path scrolls sideways and keeps the open folder in view. With `onSubmit`, a click on the field's empty part or a double-click turns it into a text box holding `value`: Enter goes there, Escape or leaving it puts the path back. A quiet path under a composer is PathLine instead. | layout/PathField.tsx |
| `FramedPage` | Every page's frame, as Kura's window: its toolbar rows across the top and its side columns (a rail or sidebar at the start, a side panel or preview at the end) on the sidebar's color, so with Misty's own sidebar they read as one frame; the page's work between them on the page's color. A hairline closes each toolbar row and a seam parts each column from the work; dragging a seam resizes the column. Nothing floats over the work. Popups, dialogs and the narrow glance card (`SideCard floating`) are the only things above it. | layout/FramedPage.tsx |
| `SectionHeading` | The heading over a group of rows: a Space home section, the sidebar's chat sections, a chat's Channels and Direct messages. Plain muted text, not a chip, 36px tall and aligned with the rows under it, with an optional count, one action at the right end and an optional fold. Only the fold button washes on hover. | layout/SectionHeading.tsx |
| `SidePanel` | The side column a page docks beside its work, such as a chat's files, changes, terminal or browser: flush beside it on the frame's color (the sidebar's), parted by a hairline seam down its leading edge, as a FramedPage's columns are. It takes width from the column before it (its previous sibling), never below `keep` for that column; the person drags the seam to resize it. The header's expand button makes it cover that column entirely, until it is restored. | layout/SidePanel.tsx |
| `SidePanelHeader` | The open view's own controls, drawn in its SidePanel's header row instead of a first row of its own. Outside a SidePanel it renders in place. | layout/SidePanel.tsx |
| `SidePanelLead` | The control a side panel's header opens with, such as the files tab's folder picker or the changes tab's branch picker. The header starts it where the rows below start their wash, and its text sits where their icons and names start, so the picked name lines up with the list under it. | layout/SidePanel.tsx |
| `SideCard` | A narrow glance column, as wide as a phone's sidebar. Docked, it is a side column on the frame's color parted by a seam; `floating`, it is the one card left over the work: at the column's top right corner (clear of its scrollbar), only as tall as what it holds, scrolling past the window, taking none of the column's width. A floating card's parent is the positioned column it floats in. | layout/SidePanel.tsx |
| `PageStage` | Where one of Misty's native pages is placed: an area the page runtime measures and puts the live page over. Until the page is on screen the host paints the page's color (base.css); once it is, nothing here is opaque, so the page shows through a menu or dialog opened over it. | layout/PageStage.tsx |
| `ScrollArea` | _No doc comment yet._ | layout/ScrollArea.tsx |
| `SidewaysScroll` | A row of a bar that scrolls sideways when its items don't fit, instead of letting them overlap or spill past its edge: no scrollbar shows (it would take the bar's room), and a mouse wheel scrolls it as a trackpad swipe does. The window's top and bottom bars hold their items in one. | layout/SidewaysScroll.tsx |
| `SplitHandle` | The seam between two resizable panes. Nothing shows at rest: the panes meet edge to edge. A wider grab area sits around the 1px seam, and a hairline shows while it is hovered, focused or dragged. `direction` is the split's: "horizontal" panes sit side by side. With `seam` the hairline shows at rest too, for panes that nothing else divides (the window's split panes). | layout/SplitHandle.tsx |
| `Separator` | _No doc comment yet._ | layout/Separator.tsx |
| `ToolbarDivider` | The hairline between two groups of controls in a bar, such as the view toggle and the sort and filter buttons. Groups sit side by side, never each in a box of its own. | layout/Separator.tsx |
| `PaneFrame` | A pane set into the window's chrome, for the window's tab panels. It keeps a margin of chrome around what it holds, `--pane-seam-top/right/bottom/left` wide (the shell's geometry writes them, and today they are 0), rounds the corners into the chrome (`--pane-corner-*`) and draws the seam line (`--pane-seam-color`), all above whatever is inside (`--layer-pane-corners`, `--layer-pane-seams`), so native pages and toolbars stay within the curve. The pane itself stays transparent, since a native page may show through it: only the margin and the corners are painted, in `--misty-window-chrome`. A hidden pane that keeps its layout (`data-tab-kept`) draws neither. | layout/PaneFrame.tsx |

Full screen it is the startup splash: the same view as an empty pane (`QuietPane`), Misty flying behind its line, never loading text; inline it is a skeleton. A full-screen one that is `leaving` fades out at once over what replaced it, so a loaded app shows right away, then calls `onLeft`. | feedback/LoadingScreen.tsx |
| `PaneLoading` | A first load whose shape isn't known until the data arrives: one spinner in the middle of its pane, shown only once the wait passes 300ms, so a quick load shows nothing at all. | feedback/PaneLoading.tsx |
| `Meter` | How full something is (an engine's context window), as a thin bar under the row that names it. Its color is what it means: neutral while there is room, amber from `high`, red from `full`. `share` runs from 0 to 1; even an empty meter shows a sliver, so it reads as a meter. | feedback/Progress.tsx |
| `Progress` | _No doc comment yet._ | feedback/Progress.tsx |
| `RingMeter` | How full something is, as a ring at the glyph size: a faint track and an arc that brightens once it passes `high` of the way. With no `value` the track is dashed: the total isn't known. It is a picture; the control holding it says what it measures. | feedback/RingMeter.tsx |
| `SetupState` | A tool getting itself ready, said in words: "Setting up the video editor". It is for the time a tool, runtime or connection takes to start (its code and engine loading, a terminal's shell or a webview starting, a live room joining, a native check), never for data, which shows a skeleton shaped like the content (`Skeleton`) or, when its shape isn't known, `PaneLoading`. When the setup fails it says so with Try again, and when it runs past `stallAfterMs` it says it is taking a while, so it never hangs without a word. | feedback/SetupState.tsx |
| `ToolSuspense` | Where a tool's code (`lazyTool`) arrives: `SetupState` says the tool is setting up while it loads, and if the code can't be fetched it says so with Try again, which fetches it afresh. Takes `SetupState`'s props for how that line reads and sits. | feedback/ToolSuspense.tsx |
| `Skeleton` | One placeholder block. Its fill is the control wash (text at 10%), so it shows on every surface it lands on: the window, the sidebar, a settings card or a dialog. | feedback/Skeleton.tsx |
| `SkeletonCode` | Lines of code with their number gutter, for an editor or a diff: monospace lines at the code view's 22.5px line height. | feedback/Skeleton.tsx |

| `SkeletonDocument` | A document page placeholder for previews and readers. | feedback/Skeleton.tsx |

Pick the `variant` the real rows use, the number of text `lines`, the `leading` picture and the `trailing` controls, so the swap doesn't move anything. A list of ListRows uses ListRowSkeleton; settings rows in a settings panel use `SettingsRowSkeleton` in the settings feature, which keeps the panel's hairlines. | feedback/Skeleton.tsx |
| `Spinner` | The one loading indicator. Spinning refresh or retry glyphs are icon states, not loaders. | feedback/Spinner.tsx |

Tabs share one width and shrink together when they don't fit, never wrapping; once they reach their least width the tabs and `after` scroll sideways (a wheel or a swipe, with no scrollbar), the open tab kept in view. `after` holds a control right after the last tab, and `end` controls at the far end that never scroll away. | navigation/TabStrip.tsx |

In the list, the header sits right on its hairline, and every column's right edge is a seam the person drags (or moves with the arrow keys) to size it, as in Kura, its line running down through the rows while the list is hovered; a double-click on a seam fits the columns to the page again. The list keeps its own step in from each side, so put it flush in its pane, with no padding around it: the header's hairline then runs to both edges and its seams meet the bar's hairline above. For Finder's column view use ColumnBrowser; for a tree, TreeRow. | patterns/collection/CollectionItems.tsx |
| `CollectionSkeleton` | Fills the collection pane while its first set of items loads, shaped like what arrives: the table's rows under its header (36px text rows, or 54px rows with a leading icon when the table shows `icons`), or the grid's cards (preview cards, or `compact` icon cards). It draws more than fit and clips, so it fills any pane without measuring it. | patterns/collection/CollectionSkeleton.tsx |
| `useCollectionView` | A collection's grid or list view. With `remember` it is kept on this device under that key; without, it lasts as long as the page. | patterns/collection/collectionMemory.ts |
| `CollectionFilterMenu` | The one filter trigger for a collection: an icon button with a count of the filters that narrow the list (sorting doesn't count), opening a menu whose picks are checkmarked. | patterns/CollectionFilterMenu.tsx |
| `useCollectionRefinement` | For fully loaded collections; paginated surfaces supply server filters instead. | patterns/CollectionFilterMenu.tsx |
| `ColumnBrowser` | Finder's column view: each open folder a 270px column of 36px rows, a chevron at the end of each folder, the folder picked in one column listed in the next, and a picked file's `preview` last. The picked rows take the row wash, stronger in the column the keyboard is in. The strip scrolls sideways and keeps its last column in view; each column scrolls on its own. A loading column shows ListRowSkeletons and a failed one a muted line. Keys: ↑ and ↓ move in a column (⇧ extends, as the caller decides), → enters the picked folder's column, ← goes back, Enter or ⌘↓ opens. Right-click opens a row's `menu`; with `drag` rows move by dragging, ⌥ copying. | patterns/ColumnBrowser.tsx |
| `RenameItemDialog` | Renames one item: a small dialog with the name field, then Cancel (quiet) and Save (primary). A failure shows under the field. Mount it with an item-specific key so a draft or a failure never carries over to the next item. | patterns/RenameItemDialog.tsx |
| `MessageActions` | The one action bar under every message: a row of 27px quiet icon buttons with tooltips, aligned to the message's edge. It shows while the message (the nearest `[data-message]` around it) is hovered or holds focus (or always, with `alwaysVisible`). A pressed toggle fills its icon. Copy confirms by swapping its icon for a check for 1.5s. | patterns/MessageActions.tsx |
| `ChannelPage` | The whole page: the channel column, then the open channel. | patterns/channel/ChannelLayout.tsx |
| `ChannelSidebar` | The channel column, on the sidebar's fill: a header naming the place, then the list. | patterns/channel/ChannelLayout.tsx |
| `ChannelSidebarHeader` | The top of the channel column: the place's name with its chevron right after it, as Discord draws it, the whole bar one button that opens its menu (`asChild` trigger). | patterns/channel/ChannelLayout.tsx |
| `ChannelMain` | The open channel on the page's own color, as the tab row and bottom bar are: its header across the top, the chat, then `side` (the member list, a thread, search results) after a line, on the same fill. | patterns/channel/ChannelLayout.tsx |
| `ChannelHeader` | The open chat's own bar, under the window's tabs, as Discord draws a channel's or a direct message's: its icon (or the person's face) and name, an optional topic, then its controls. Each pane draws its own, so a split never loses a chat's controls. `actions` are its icon buttons (calls, Threads, Pinned, Members, a ⋯ of the rest), icons only with the label as the tooltip; `end` is what stays last and never folds, such as the message search. The name fades first; then the actions give way into a ⋯ menu, lowest priority first. It never wraps. | patterns/channel/ChannelLayout.tsx |
| `ChannelWelcome` | The top of a channel's history, once the very first message is in view: a large mark, a welcome and where this channel begins. A direct message opens the same way with the person's face as its `mark` (an xl Avatar in a large PresenceFace, or a group's faces) and its name as the title, and may offer a few buttons under the line (`actions`, such as Call). | patterns/channel/ChannelLayout.tsx |
| `ChannelDivider` | A line across the history with a label in it: a day (`date`), or where the messages the person hasn't read begin (`new`), drawn in the danger color with a "New" tag at its end. | patterns/channel/ChannelLayout.tsx |
| `TypingLine` | "X is typing…" in the strip just above the composer, so it reads beside what is being written: the strip keeps its height when empty, so the history never jumps as it comes and goes. | patterns/channel/ChannelLayout.tsx |
| `MentionMark` | The mark on a message that mentions the person reading it, by name or by a role they hold: a thin bar down its left edge, in the waiting tone. The message is the positioning box. | patterns/channel/ChannelLayout.tsx |
| `MemberList` | The member list beside a channel's messages, on the channel's own fill, as Discord's. | patterns/channel/MemberList.tsx |
| `MemberGroupHeading` | A group's heading: its name, a dash and how many are in it ("Online — 3"). | patterns/channel/MemberList.tsx |
| `PresenceFace` | Someone's status as a small dot on the corner of their face, wherever a face shows (a member row, a DM, a friend): green online, amber idle, red do not disturb, nothing offline. The face and the dot sit in this box; the dot's ring is the surface's own color (`ring` is the sidebar where the face sits on the sidebar). `size="lg"` is for a large face (an xl Avatar), such as a profile's or a direct message's opening, whose dot grows with it. | patterns/channel/MemberList.tsx |
| `MemberRow` | One person: their face with a presence dot, their name in their role's color with a crown for the Space's owner, and a quiet second line (what their agent is doing). | patterns/channel/MemberList.tsx |
| `PersonProfile` | The other person's profile beside a one-to-one direct message, where a channel has its member list, as Discord shows it: their face large (a `PresenceFace` with `size="lg"`), their name, their own status line, then `PersonProfileSection`s about them. It sits in `ChannelMain`'s `side`, on the chat's own fill, and carries no banner. A group's people are a `MemberList` instead. | patterns/channel/PersonProfile.tsx |
| `PersonProfileSection` | One part of a `PersonProfile` under its muted heading, such as Friends since. | patterns/channel/PersonProfile.tsx |
| `ChannelMessage` | One message in a channel. `grouped` folds it under the sender's previous message: no face or name, its short time in the face's column on hover. `tools` are the message's own buttons (reactions, reply, edit, its ⋯), drawn 27px in a small bar at its top right while it is hovered, holds focus or has a menu open (`active`). `mentioned` marks a message that names the reader; `editing` washes the one being edited; `pending` dims one still being sent. | patterns/channel/ChannelMessage.tsx |
| `ChannelMessageText` | A message's text: body type that keeps its line breaks and wraps long words. `jumbo` sets a message of only a few emoji large, as Discord does; `edited` adds the quiet "(edited)" after it, with when in its tooltip. | patterns/channel/ChannelMessage.tsx |
| `ChannelReply` | The line over a message that answers another: a bent arrow from the face's column, the original's sender (an 18px face and their name) and one line of what they said, the whole line a button that brings the original into view. `missing` says the original isn't drawn: still further back (`earlier`) or deleted. | patterns/channel/ChannelMessage.tsx |
| `ChannelReactions` | The reactions under a message, in a row that wraps: each a ReactionChip, then, for someone who may react, the button that opens the emoji picker (`add`, usually an EmojiPicker's trigger). | patterns/channel/ChannelMessage.tsx |
| `ReactionChip` | One reaction: the emoji and how many gave it, pressed (`mine`) when the reader is one of them. Pressing it adds or takes back the reader's own. | patterns/channel/ChannelMessage.tsx |
| `AddReactionButton` | The button after the reactions that opens the emoji picker. Forwards its props to IconButton. | patterns/channel/ChannelMessage.tsx |
| `ThreadRepliesButton` | How many replies a message's thread has, as a quiet button that opens the thread. | patterns/channel/ChannelMessage.tsx |
| `CallStage` | Where a call's people are seen, as Discord's voice channel and call views draw them: every tile shares the stage, in columns that fit how many there are (one fills it, two side by side, then a grid, up to eight), with an odd last tile in a pair of columns taking the whole row. With `focus`, that tile fills the stage and the rest sit in a strip beside it. It fills its parent; the call's controls (`CallBar`) go under it. | patterns/call/CallStage.tsx |
| `CallTile` | One person in a call, in a `CallStage`: their camera or shared screen filling a rounded tile, else their face in the middle of a quiet well, and their name at its foot on a dark chip so it reads over any picture. Whoever is talking is ringed in the done tone. The tile's own buttons (full screen, stop watching) show on hover at its top right. | patterns/call/CallStage.tsx |
| `CallBar` | A call's controls in one centered row under its `CallStage`, the same in every place the call shows (a voice channel's page, a DM, full screen). It never wraps; Leave, the one danger button, comes last. | patterns/call/CallStage.tsx |
| `EmojiPicker` | The emoji picker: a search on top, a row of jump buttons for its sections, then the emoji in a grid under their headings, and the one under the pointer named along the bottom. It brings no emoji of its own: the caller hands in its `sections` (empty while they load, drawn as a skeleton) and its `search`, and remembers what was picked. Shift-click picks without closing. Open it from its child (the trigger), or, with `anchor`, from anything that sets `open`, such as a menu's "Add reaction". | patterns/EmojiPicker.tsx |
| `QuestionPanel` | A question or approval waiting on the person, flat between hairlines above the composer: what is asked, the choices, then the buttons in one row. Questions from Misty, from an outside engine and from an action that needs an OK all use it. | patterns/QuestionPanel.tsx |
| `FindBar` | Find (and replace) docked at the top of a document: a flat row under a hairline with the field, case, whole word and pattern toggles, where the search is (`2/7`), stepping and close. The toggles fold into ⋯ first when the pane is narrow, then select all, then stepping. | patterns/FindBar.tsx |
| `ImageCropFrame` | The crop drawn over an image: the kept part clear inside a bright edge, the rest dimmed, with corner and edge handles to size it and the middle to move it. While it is dragged, thirds lines show. Its parent is the image's own box (positioned, the image's size); the crop is in fractions of it, so it holds its place as the image scales. | patterns/ImageCropFrame.tsx |
| `ShapeSelection` | The frame around shapes picked on a canvas (an image's marks): a bright outline along the selection's edge, which may be turned with the canvas, and square handles to size it by. `tone` draws someone else's selection in their color, with no handles; `dashed` is the box being dragged out to pick shapes. It fills its positioned parent and takes the pointer only on its handles. | patterns/ShapeSelection.tsx |
| `ZoomControl` | Zoom out, the zoom level, zoom in: one tight group in a bar, as Preview's. The level opens a menu of set levels (`children`, MenuItems). The three sit close together so they read as one control, apart from the bar's other buttons. | patterns/ZoomControl.tsx |
| `MediaPlayerCard` | A media player, laid out like Zen's: the track's artwork and title with the card's own buttons at the top, a position bar that can be dragged, and the transport in the middle beneath it, between the source's mark and a mute button. Previous restarts the track when the source has no previous one; the bar shows only for a finite length. `compact` folds all but the track away. Monochrome: the only color is the artwork and the source's mark. | patterns/MediaPlayerCard.tsx |
| `StarterPrompts` | Ideas to start from under an empty chat, for someone who doesn't know what to ask yet: quiet rows of an icon and a label in two columns as wide as their labels, the whole block centered under the heading. It drops to one column before a label would be cut. Picking one hands its prompt to the caller, which puts it in the composer unsent. | patterns/StarterPrompts.tsx |
| `TurnFold` | The turn's one line: what it is doing while it runs (with a moving highlight), what it did once it ends. It opens to the turn's steps; `more` says how many earlier steps a live turn keeps folded above the latest ones. | patterns/ToolTimeline.tsx |
| `ToolList` | The turn's steps, one row each with no gap between them. | patterns/ToolTimeline.tsx |
| `ToolRow` | One step on one 36px line: its icon, what it did (muted), what it acted on (full color, fading at the edge), and its end (a duration, a count, line changes). It has no fill or border. A row that opens swaps its icon for a chevron on hover; a running step is dimmed, a failed one red. Render it inside a ToolList `li`, with its ToolBody after it. | patterns/ToolTimeline.tsx |
| `ToolPath` | A path as a row shows it: the folder muted, the file's name in full color. | patterns/ToolTimeline.tsx |
| `ToolLines` | Lines a step added and removed, in their own colors, each with its sign. | patterns/ToolTimeline.tsx |
| `ToolBody` | What an opened row shows, hanging off a thin line under the row's icon. The line folds the row again when pressed. Code inside keeps its own monospace; prose is the row's size. | patterns/ToolTimeline.tsx |
| `ToolNote` | What the agent wrote between steps: quiet prose at the rows' size. | patterns/ToolTimeline.tsx |
| `ModelPicker` | The model and how hard it thinks, as two buttons side by side (after OpenChamber's): the model opens a search over the models, one name per row and a check on the current one; a model picked runs at the level last used with it. The level is its own button and menu, shown only for a model that takes levels. | patterns/ModelPicker.tsx |
| `StepPage` | A page of a few steps on the window's surface, such as first-run setup: Back and the steps' progress, the step's heading, its content in one centered column, and the buttons that move on. The page scrolls when the step is taller than the window. | patterns/StepPage.tsx |
| `HeroPage` | A page that greets, such as the first-run welcome: a large heading with its tagline and the page's buttons in the middle of the window, and a line of small print along the bottom. The heading grows with the window. | patterns/HeroPage.tsx |
| `AppTile` | One installed app on a Space home: its logo over its name, washing under the pointer. | patterns/home/AppTile.tsx |
| `AddAppTile` | The tile that ends a grid on a Space home: a dashed square with a plus, then what it adds ("Add app" by default, "New agent" after the agents). | patterns/home/AppTile.tsx |
| `AgentTile` | One agent on a Space home, in the apps' grid: its face over its name, then one quiet line of what it is doing ("Writing the launch plan", "Needs you", or whose it is). While it works its face breathes a blue dot at the corner; while it waits on the person, an amber one. | patterns/home/AppTile.tsx |
| `AppLauncher` | The apps of a Space in one launcher over the window, as macOS's Applications in Spotlight: a large search on top, then every app as an AppTile in a grid that scrolls, however many a Space adds. Typing narrows the tiles and Enter opens the first (`onSubmit`); Escape or a click outside closes it. The caller filters; the launcher lays it out. | patterns/home/AppLauncher.tsx |
| `HomeSectionHead` | The one heading every block on a Space's home wears: a title, its count, an optional dot when something waits for the person, and an action at the far end. | patterns/home/HomeSection.tsx |
| `HomeSection` | A block of a Space's home: its heading, then whatever it holds. `panel` sets it in a card with a hairline edge, for the overview's blocks that sit two to a row, so they read as their own places on the page. `divided` draws a hairline above it, for the block that starts a new part of the page (the Space's own things under its overview). | patterns/home/HomeSection.tsx |
| `OverviewDot` | A chat's or run's state as a small dot in its color: blue and breathing while it works, amber while it waits on the person, red when it failed. | patterns/home/HomeSection.tsx |
| `PlaceChip` | A page or topic on a home, as a small chip: its icon, then its name, on a faint fill with no edge, washing under the pointer. A row of them wraps (`homeChipsClass`), so the home reads as a page rather than a grid of boxes. `pressed` marks the one picked, for chips that pick (the Lab's topics); chips that open a page leave it out. | patterns/home/HomeSection.tsx |
| `ItemCard` | One thing in a Space as a card, the one card every page of the Space shows things in (the home's docs and drawings, the Lab's notebooks): a cover that previews it, then under the cover, on the page itself, the kind's glyph and its title, one quiet line about it, and a foot for who made it and what's happening. The cover is the card's only shape, as an album or a file in Finder: no box around the words. It lifts under the pointer; a picked card's cover takes a strong edge. Controls over the card (a menu) come as children, outside its press area, over the cover. | patterns/home/ItemCard.tsx |
| `MessageComposer` | The message box every chat uses. Layout only: feature adapters keep drafts, uploads, mentions and sending. The text grows with its content, the bar under it gives way instead of wrapping, and the path line sits under the box. | patterns/MessageComposer.tsx |
| `MessageComposerSend` | The send button every composer shares, the height of every other control in the composer's row (controls in one row share one height); a running agent can put its Stop button (the same size) there instead. | patterns/MessageComposer.tsx |
| `MessageComposerAction` | A button that takes the send button's place, such as Stop while a reply runs: a solid square like Send, in a soft wash instead of Send's bright fill, so the slot keeps its size and shape. The tools beside Send (voice input, mention, emoji) are plain quiet IconButtons, washed only under the pointer. | patterns/MessageComposer.tsx |
| `ComposerStatusRow` | One row at the top of a card composer, about the chat's state: a muted glyph, what it says (fading at the edge), and its actions at the end. 36px, with a hairline under all but the last; the row makes its actions 27px, buttons and icon buttons alike. | patterns/MessageComposer.tsx |
| `ComposerAttachment` | A file waiting to go with the message, in the composer's `context` row: its kind's glyph, its name (fading when long) and a × that takes it off. For pictures shown as thumbnails, a chat draws its own tile. | patterns/MessageComposer.tsx |
| `usePointerDropTarget` | Pointer-only gestures never enter Tauri's native file/HTML drag loop. | hooks/pointerDropTargets.ts |
| `usePointerDrag` | Starts a drag from a pointerdown, or from a pointermove with the primary button held, so a control can first decide what a gesture is (a pull versus a reorder) and hand off. | hooks/usePointerReorder.ts |
| `usePointerReorder` | _No doc comment yet._ | hooks/usePointerReorder.ts |
| `useNow` | The current time, for anything shown relative to it. React re-renders on state, and time passing is no state change, so a "3m" computed from `Date.now()` during render stays "3m" until something else happens to re-render it. This is that missing event: one local clock for the whole app (never a request to anything), moving on each step while the window is visible and catching up as soon as it is seen again. Every component on the same step re-renders together. | hooks/useNow.ts |
